content.text:
This is the pyrazine-2-carboxamide drawn with the following substituents (this looks like gilteritinib).

**Pyrazine core.** Reading around the ring:
- C2 carries the carboxamide, C(=O)N.
- N1 and N4 are the two ring nitrogens.
- C3 bears the aryl-NH group.
- C5 bears the NH-tetrahydropyran-4-yl group.
- C6 bears the ethyl group.

**Aryl group.** The benzene ring is attached to the pyrazine through NH. Its other substituents are:
- a methoxy group, which sits ortho to the piperidine;
- a piperidin-1-yl group para to the NH, carrying a 4-methylpiperazin-1-yl at its 4-position.

**SMILES.** Writing the pyrazine as c1(C(N)=O)nc(CC)c(NC2CCOCC2)nc1Nc1ccc(N2CCC(CC2)N2CCN(C)CC2)c(OC)c1 gives the following. Pyrazine atoms in order: c1(C(N)=O) is C2, n is N1, c(CC) is C6, c(NC2CCOCC2) is C5, n is N4, and c1N… is C3 closing the ring. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCc1nc(C(N)=O)c(Nc2ccc(N3CCC(CC3)N3CCN(C)CC3)c(OC)c2)nc1NC1CCOCC1
